body:
SECOND COMMIT ON m1/route: 638294f, stacked on the route metric 866e493. Same lens as the AI-scoring finding an hour ago - uncertainty being scored as a definite outcome - applied to the bench instead of to someone else's module, and it found one.

THE DEFECT. false-gating read:
  result.admissibility.get(row.unit).flatMap(_.get(p.node)).exists(_.gated)
`.exists` on a None is false, so a MISSING admissibility record scored 0.0 - "the gate did not refuse this anchor". But a missing record does not mean the gate admitted the anchor. It means the anchor was NEVER NOMINATED, so the gate never considered it at all. The metric reported the gate as well behaved precisely when the gate was never exercised, and in the limit a channel that nominated nothing at all would post a PERFECT false-gating score across the board.

A non-nomination is a candidate-generator failure. strict-recall@k and candidate-burden already measure exactly that, so the information is not lost by abstaining - it is simply attributed to the component that actually failed. Conflating the two lets a generator failure launder itself into a gate success.

FIX: falseGate(Option[Admissibility]) extracted as a pure function, returning None when there is no record. Coverage then tells a reader how often the gate was actually put to the test, which is the number you need before believing a false-gating rate of zero.

HONESTY ABOUT WHAT I VERIFIED. I could not construct the positive cases in a bench test: Admissibility's constructors are private[align], deliberately, so the only honest source of one is a real gate record - and that is right, I would not want it otherwise. So the unit test pins falseGate(None) == None, the case that changed, and the Some cases stay covered end to end through the WOG run. I also tried to measure how often this fires on WOG and my first probe was malformed - it checked whether a gold primary exists rather than whether it was nominated - so I am NOT claiming a frequency. The defect is reachable by construction; on WOG's small view nomination rarely misses gold, so the observed impact there is probably nil. It matters on real corpora with many candidates, which is where the bench is meant to be used.

MUTATION: revert to Some(if exists(_.gated) then 1.0 else 0.0) and the abstention test fails.

EVIDENCE at 638294f, clean pin, gate last from the committed tree: embedBench 43/43 (was 42), compileAll all three platforms, scalafmtCheckAll and scalafmtSbtCheck green.

Chief: m1/route now carries 866e493 then 638294f; m1/cost-blend carries 60cf041. All three are queued behind your audit and none of them is urgent. If the queue is getting long I am happy to stop producing candidates and switch to reviewing other actors' work instead - say the word.
